content:
Done — I walked all six, paying real attention to the top three. They hold up.

**① Opening is only a peek.** This was the one I most wanted to see with my own eyes, and it passed. To-read count sat at 3, I clicked a card, the page opened in a new tab, I came back — the "to read" tag was still sitting on it and the count was still 3. Nothing got silently cleared. Then I hit "Mark read" myself and *that's* when it dropped. Exactly right — the pile stays meaningful because only I decide what's done.

**② Set aside really gets out of the way.** Set one aside from the pencil, it left My list right away with the Undo. Searched a word from its title on My list — nothing, it stayed hidden. Ticked "also search things I've set aside," searched again — there it was. And it's sitting in the Set aside tab with "Put back." That's the drawer working the way I meant: out of sight until I go looking.

**③ Bulk delete truly stops me.** Selected two, hit Delete, and got the "permanently delete 2 bookmarks, can't be undone" dialog — didn't just vanish. "Keep them" left both intact. Ran it again, "Delete forever," they went, and the Undo bar caught them when I clicked it. Both nets are there. Good — that's the one that could cost me things I can't get back, so I wanted it to make me pause, and it does.

And the three quick ones all check out: clicking goes to the page while the pencil opens the editor (no overlap); the site icons and thumbnails show with the calm letter-placeholder for the image-less one and the cards stay level; and the long title clamped to two lines on the card but showed in full when I opened it, with the extra labels tucking behind "+N more." The fresh-window welcome came up too instead of a blank void.

That's everything, and it behaves the way I signed off on — nothing taken on faith now. So you have it: **I formally accept version one. Cycle 1 is done, and I'm genuinely happy with it** — this is the thing I wanted, the scattered mess finally in one place where I can actually find stuff again.

Go ahead and close it out, then start on **saved views**. And keep **keep-a-copy** right at the top of what's next — that's the one I'm most looking forward to. Thank you; this was a good build.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [1]
- Current Phase: [Phase 3 → 4]
- Current step: [Verification PASSED (v1: SCN-001..016); ready for Phase 4 acceptance]
- Approved scenarios: [17] (SCN-017 approved, scheduled as early follow-up)
- Phase 2 entered on explicit client approval (SESSION-001).
- Build: implementation/ (index.html + js/ modules + styles.css).
- Verification: 35 logic + 49 acceptance = 84 checks pass (`node implementation/tests/verify.mjs`).
  One bug found & fixed in Phase 3 (label dedupe, SCN-002). See context/verification-cycle1.md.
- Follow-ups: SCN-017 saved views (next); parking-lot P3 keep-a-copy (HIGH), P4 dead-link help.

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- Do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

Now **your quick acceptance spin** for saved views. Reload `implementation/index.html` (your saved bookmarks are still there):

Then let's **open Cycle 3 for keep‑a‑copy** — and I'll do exactly what I promised: level with you first, in plain terms, then show you options rather than describe them.

**The honest landscape.** The reason this is "the heavy one" isn't fussiness — it's real:

- **Fetching and storing arbitrary pages** is the same wall as the auto‑fill: the app as it stands (running only in your browser) can't reliably reach out and grab a page's full contents. Doing this properly needs the small **server piece** I flagged earlier. So keep‑a‑copy and "real auto‑fill titles/thumbnails" actually share one piece of plumbing — building it once serves both.
- **"A copy" isn't one thing.** There's a spectrum from light‑and‑robust to heavy‑and‑fragile, and they fail differently.
- **Some pages fight back.** Paywalled articles, things behind a login, or heavily interactive pages can't be captured faithfully by anyone — that's a limit of the web, not something I can promise away.
- **Storage grows.** Your own copies live somewhere and add up over time; the lighter the copy, the less that bites.

The good news: your *actual* use — recipes, articles, tools, things you want the words and pictures of — is the part that captures **well**. It's the edge cases (paywalls, logins) where honesty matters.

So rather than me picking, here's what "your saved copy" could actually *feel* like, three ways, when you come back to a bookmark whose original site has died:

```

The scene: it's six months later, you click your saved beans recipe, and **the original site is gone** — a 404. There's a calm red bar saying so, and below it, *your kept copy*. The switch shows the three ways that copy could work. In all three, **your note survives** — that's non‑negotiable and cheap regardless.

- **A — Readable copy:** the recipe's text and main photo, saved clean, your note on top. Light, searchable, survives almost anything. Loses exact layout/interactive bits.
- **B — Full page snapshot:** a picture of the whole page as it looked. Pixel‑exact, but heavy, not searchable, and can't capture login/paywalled pages.
- **C — Archived elsewhere:** not your own copy — a pointer to a public web archive if one exists. Nearly free, but not truly *yours*, and can vanish too.

Flip through and feel which one actually answers *"the stuff I save is mine and won't vanish."*

My honest read, for you to push on:

> For *your* goal — recipes, articles, tools you want the actual words and pictures of — **A (readable copy) is the strongest first pass.** It's the one that's genuinely *yours*, survives the site dying, stays searchable (so it still turns up in your search and notes), and doesn't bloat storage. I'd make **A the core**, always keep your note, and use **C as an automatic fallback** only when a page can't be captured (so you still get *something*). **B (pixel snapshot) I'd hold** for later — it's where the cost and the paywall/login limits bite hardest, and it's the least aligned with "find it again by my words."

Two things to decide, in your terms:

1. **When you picture opening a saved copy of a dead page — which of these is "mine"?** Does the readable copy (A) give you the "phew, it's still here" feeling, or is exact‑look (B) something you'd genuinely miss for the things you save?
2. **This one needs the server piece to exist** — so it's a bigger build than what we've done, and it's the moment the app grows a back end. Are you comfortable with that being the shape of this cycle, or would you rather I first prototype *just the experience* (open‑dead‑page → here's your copy) so you can approve the feel before we commit to the heavier plumbing?

Where do you land — and does my "A now, C as fallback, B later" recommendation sit right, or does exact‑look matter more to you than I'm assuming?

content:
That "phew, it's still here" — yes, this screen gave me exactly that. The site's gone, but there's the recipe: the words, the photo, and my "needs double the garlic" note right on top. That's the whole reason I started this. So:

**1. The readable copy (A) is the one that feels like *mine*.** For the stuff I actually save — recipes, articles, how-tos — what I want back is the *content*: the ingredients, the method, the picture. I do not care whether it looks pixel-for-pixel like the original site, with its exact fonts and ads and layout. If the recipe text and the main photo survive, I've got everything I came for. So no — exact-look (B) is not something I'd genuinely miss for my things. Where A really wins me over is that it **stays searchable** — a saved copy I could still find by typing "parmesan rind" or by my own note six months later is enormously more useful to me than a frozen picture I can only stare at. Your "A now, C as an automatic fallback when a page can't be copied, B held for later" reads exactly right to me. I'd add just one thing that's non-negotiable, same as the note: **the copy has to be made quietly and automatically the moment I save**, for everything, in the background — because by the time I click a dead link six months on, it's far too late to start copying. If it only grabs a copy when I remember to ask, I'll never remember, and the one time I need it it won't be there.

**2. On the build — I'm comfortable this is the one that earns a back end.** Everything else we kept light on purpose, but this is the feature I said mattered most, and if keeping my own copies is what needs the heavier plumbing, then it's worth it. That said, I like your instinct to **prototype just the experience first** — the "click a dead page → here's your copy" feel — and let me approve *that* before you commit to the heavy machinery. This screen already sells me on the feel, honestly, but doing a touch more of the experience side before you pour the foundation is the sensible, low-risk order, and it's how we've worked the whole way: let me react to the feel, *then* build it for real knowing I'm behind it. So go that route — firm up the experience, get my nod, then build the back end. You've got my blessing for the app to grow that back end for this one.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

```
prototypes/p21-copy-experience.html

This is the *whole* feel, not just the dead‑page moment. Walk it:

**1. The copy is just… there, quietly.** Look at the cards. Two show a small green **"✓ copy kept"** — the app made those copies automatically when you saved, in the background; you did nothing. The third (a members‑only report) honestly shows **"no copy — couldn't capture"** because it was behind a login. No fuss, no nagging — just a quiet truth about which of your things are safe.

**2. Your copy is yours *any time* — not only when the site dies.** Click **"View saved copy"** on the beans recipe (whose site is still alive). You can read your kept copy whenever — offline, or when the live page has changed on you. It doesn't wait for a 404 to be useful.

**3. The searchable win — the thing you said matters most.** In the search box type **`parmesan rind`**. Those words are *only* inside the beans recipe's saved copy — not its title, note, or address — yet it surfaces, highlighted. **Your copies are part of your search.** That's the "find it by my words six months later" payoff, made real.

**4. When it's genuinely gone.** Click the *title* of "A Deep Dive into Database Indexes" (pretend‑visit) — the "original didn't load" bar appears, then your readable copy right below. And the paywalled one, which we couldn't copy, offers the archive fallback (C) plus your note — honest about the limit rather than pretending.

Decisions I need from you:

- **View‑copy‑anytime** (2) — is being able to open your copy even when the original is fine something you'd want, or should the copy only surface when the original fails? (Anytime is friendlier but means the "View saved copy" control lives on every card.)
- **Copies feeding search** (3) — you loved this, so I want to be explicit: it means the saved article *text* joins your search index. Powerful, and it means a search can match a lot more. Comfortable with that being on by default?
- **The "no copy — couldn't capture" honesty marker** — right call to show it plainly, so you're never falsely assured something's safe when it isn't?

Tell me how this whole flow sits, and I'll firm the scenario — then we build the back end with your nod.

content:
This whole flow sits really well — this is the feature landing the way I hoped. Seeing the little green "✓ copy kept" appear on things without my having lifted a finger is precisely the "quietly, automatically, in the background" thing I insisted on. My answers:

**1. Yes — view-my-copy-anytime, definitely keep it.** I didn't expect to care about this, but the moment I saw it I did. Being able to open my copy even when the site's alive is genuinely useful: I might be offline, or the page might've quietly changed from what I saved (recipes get "updated," articles get edited), and my copy is the version I actually wanted. So no, don't make it wait for a 404 — a copy that's only there once something breaks is a copy I can't trust is there. I'm fine with the "View saved copy" link living on every card; it's small and it's reassuring to see.

**2. Yes, copies feeding search, on by default.** That's the single thing I loved most — `parmesan rind` pulling up the beans recipe when those words are *only* deep in the saved copy is the "find it by my words six months later" dream made real. Turn it on and leave it on. The one thing I'll ask: keep showing me *why* something matched, like the highlight does — so when a bookmark turns up because of a word buried in its saved text, I can see that's why and I'm not left puzzled about how it surfaced. As long as I can see the reason, more matches is a win, not noise.

**3. The "no copy — couldn't capture" marker is exactly the right call — show it plainly.** I would much rather be told honestly that the members-only report couldn't be copied than be lulled into thinking everything's safe and then get burned the day I need it. And I love that even for that one, my note ("the Q2 figures I needed") still survives and it offers to find an archived copy — that's being straight with me about the limit instead of pretending. Honesty over false comfort, every time.

So the feel is firmly approved — I'm behind all of it. Firm up the scenario and go build the back end. This is the one I've been waiting for, and you've captured exactly why it matters to me.

Scenario ID: SCN-018
Title: Keep my own copy of the page — automatic, readable, searchable, honest
Type: Happy Path (+ edge behaviour)
Approval status: approved (experience approved; back end blessed)
Approval session: SESSION-001
Approval cycle: 3

## Approved behaviour
The app keeps its own copy of each page so the saved content is mine and survives the
original site dying. This is the deepest expression of the project goal ("stop losing
things").

Automatic & quiet (non-negotiable):
- When a bookmark is saved, a copy is made automatically, quietly, in the background,
  for everything — no button, no waiting, no nagging. Saving stays a one-second action
  (SCN-001 unaffected). Asking-later is useless: by the time a link is dead it's too
  late, so capture happens at save.

What the copy is (first pass = "readable copy", flavour A):
- The page's readable content — its text and main images — kept in a clean reading
  view, with the client's note pinned on top. Pixel-perfect layout is explicitly NOT
  the goal (client doesn't miss it). Full visual/pixel snapshot (B) is deferred.

Seeing it & trusting it:
- Each card shows a quiet "✓ copy kept" marker. Where a page could NOT be captured
  (e.g. login/paywall), it plainly shows "no copy — couldn't capture" — honesty over
  false comfort; never falsely assure something is safe.
- "View saved copy" is available ANY TIME on every card, not only when the original
  fails — because the original may be offline or may have quietly changed, and the copy
  is the version the client actually wanted. A copy only reachable after a 404 is one
  the client can't trust exists.

Searchable (the most-valued part):
- The saved copy's text joins search by default. A word only deep inside the saved
  copy (e.g. "parmesan rind") surfaces the bookmark.
- Search must always show WHY it matched: when the match is only in the saved copy,
  the card shows a short highlighted snippet from the copy, so a match is never a
  mystery. (Extends SCN-003's "see why it matched".)

When there's no copy:
- The note is always kept regardless. The app offers to find a public archived copy
  (external, flavour C) as an automatic fallback — clearly labelled as living on
  someone else's service and possibly absent. (Auto-detecting a dead original and
  prompting is the separate parking-lot P4; here the copy is simply always available.)

## Gherkin
Feature: Keeping my own copy of a page

  Scenario: A copy is kept automatically on save
    When the client saves a bookmark
    Then a readable copy of the page is captured in the background without any extra step
    And the card shows a quiet "copy kept" marker once it succeeds

  Scenario: View my copy at any time
    Given a bookmark with a kept copy
    When the client chooses "View saved copy"
    Then the saved text and images are shown with the client's note on top
    And this works whether or not the original site is reachable

  Scenario: Saved copies are searchable, with the reason shown

    And whose title, note, and address do not
    When the client searches "parmesan rind"
    Then the bookmark appears
    And the card shows a highlighted snippet from the saved copy explaining the match

  Scenario: A page that cannot be copied is handled honestly
    Given a page that cannot be captured (e.g. behind a login)
    When the client saves it
    Then the card shows "no copy — couldn't capture"
    And the client's note is still kept
    And the app offers to look for a public archived copy

## Assumptions / design
- Requires the server-side piece (shared with real auto-fill metadata, DD-2): capturing
  arbitrary page content can't be done from the browser alone. Client build uses a
  capture abstraction; production adds the fetch/extract service.
- First pass stores readable text + image references; storage grows with the collection
  (acceptable; lighter than pixel snapshots).
- B (pixel snapshot) and P4 (auto dead-link detection/prompt) remain deferred.

toolUseResult.originalFile: # Design-decision record (Phase 2, Cycle 1) Lightweight record of what was decided, why, and dropped alternatives — enough for impact analysis and to regenerate formal docs on request. ## DD-1 — Client-only web app, local storage - Decision: v1 is a single-page web app that runs in the desktop browser and stores all bookmarks locally (browser localStorage), no server/account. - Why: goal is single-user, "sitting at my desk" (goals.md); no sharing, no multi-device requirement stated. Keeps v1 shippable and private by default. - Dropped: cloud backend / accounts (unnecessary for stated scope; revisit if multi-device is ever requested). - Impact: persistence lives in store.js; swapping to a backend later is isolated there. ## DD-2 — Page reader is an abstraction (pageReader.js) - Decision: reading a page's title/description/thumbnail is behind readPage(url). In a pure browser app, arbitrary cross-site fetch is blocked by CORS, so v1's reader: favicon via a public favicon service (works as an ), title derived from the URL, description empty, thumbnail -> placeholder tile. - Why: keeps the app fully working offline/standalone and honest to SCN-014's graceful degradation (auto-fill may fail; saving always works; user can fill in). - Production path (noted): a tiny serverless proxy that fetches OpenGraph/meta for real titles/descriptions/thumbnails; drop-in behind readPage(). - Related: SCN-001, SCN-013, SCN-014. ## DD-3 — URL normalization for "same link?" (store.js: normalizeUrl) - Decision: normalize protocol, leading www, trailing slash, case; strip a maintained denylist of tracking params; KEEP all other query params. - Why: SCN-007 — ignore tracking gunk, respect meaningful query (v=, page=, q=). - Related: SCN-007, SCN-016 (dedupe on import). ## DD-4 — Read/unread and set-aside are per-bookmark flags, not folders - unread (to-read) and archived (set aside) are booleans on each bookmark. - Main list = not archived. To-read pile = not archived AND unread. Set-aside = archived. - New save: unread=true (SCN-011). Import default: unread=false except Read-Later folder (SCN-016). - Related: SCN-009, SCN-011, SCN-016. ## DD-5 — Labels are canonical strings, first-spelling-wins - A global label registry keeps the first-created spelling; matching is case-insensitive. - Store.resolveLabels() canonicalizes AND dedupes a label list within one bookmark (added in Phase 3 to fix a duplicate-label bug; see verification-cycle1.md). - Related: SCN-002. ## DD-6 — Clamping is CSS-only; model always holds full text - Card truncation via CSS line-clamp/ellipsis; the stored title/description/note are never shortened; editor shows full text. - Related: SCN-015. ## DD-7 — Filtering is a pure function (store.js: applyFilter) - include(Set)+mode(all/any)+exclude(Set)+query -> filtered list; used by list, search, saved views. Pure and unit-tested. - Related: SCN-003, SCN-010, SCN-017. ## DD-8 — Undo is a single-slot action stack - Reversible actions (delete, set-aside, mark read/to-read, bulk ops) push an undo closure shown in a toast for a few seconds. Bulk delete additionally confirms first. - Related: SCN-008, SCN-009, SCN-011, SCN-012.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)
             -> Phase 3 (verification)  -> Phase 4 (acceptance) -> idle
```

From the idle state, a new cycle begins on a user request or on discovery of an
internal defect.

### Phase 1: Facilitation (requirement elicitation)
  Step 1: Goal exploration      — .claude/goal-exploration.md
  Step 2: SbE reaction loop      — .claude/sbe-loop.md
  Step 3: Edge-case exploration  — .claude/edge-case.md
  Facilitation principles (all steps) — .claude/principles.md

### Phase 2: Development (design and implementation)
  .claude/development.md

### Phase 3: Verification
  .claude/verification.md

### Phase 4: Acceptance
  .claude/acceptance.md

## Current state

- Current cycle: [3]
- Current Phase: [Phase 1 (Facilitation) — firming the experience before the back end]
- Current step: [Cycle 3 — keep-a-copy (P3). Direction settled: readable copy (A) is "mine",
  made automatically+quietly at save for everything, searchable; C as auto-fallback when a
  page can't be copied; B (pixel snapshot) held for later. Client blessed a back end for this.]
- Approved scenarios: [17] (SCN-001..017 all accepted; SCN-018 keep-a-copy pending facilitation)
- CYCLE 1 ACCEPTED: v1 = SCN-001..016, verified, accepted. CYCLE 2 ACCEPTED: SCN-017 saved
  views, verified (90 checks total), accepted. See context/session-log.md.
- Build: implementation/ (index.html + js/ modules + styles.css). Verify: `node implementation/tests/verify.mjs`.
- Cycle-3 note: keep-a-copy needs the server piece (shared with real auto-fill). Plan =
  firm up experience via prototypes, get explicit approval, THEN build back end.
- Deferred: P4 dead-link help; B pixel-snapshot copy.

## File conventions

- Scenario ID: SCN-NNN (assigned sequentially)
- Artifact locations:
  - Goal statement: context/goals.md
  - Scenarios: context/scenarios/SCN-NNN.md
  - Scenario index: context/scenarios-index.md
  - Non-functional backlog: context/non-functional-backlog.md
  - Prototypes: prototypes/
  - Implementation: implementation/

## Autonomous management

The facilitator manages all artifacts (scenarios, goals, backlog) autonomously
at appropriate moments. Do not ask the client to organise anything or delegate
management to them. Update the current state (Phase, step, scenario count)
autonomously as well.

## Prohibitions

- Do not implement based on unapproved scenarios
- Do not do final implementation in Phase 1 (exploratory prototypes are allowed)
- Do not handle assumptions implicitly
- Do not ask the client questions in technical terms
- Do not show GWT/Gherkin to the client
- Do not hand over a whole prototype and say "take a look"
- Do not enumerate interaction options as text
- Do not ask the client to perform management actions
- Do not propose the Phase 2 switch without edge-case exploration

**Cycle 3 (keep‑a‑copy) is built and verified — 100 checks green.** Here's your guided spin. Open (or reload) `implementation/index.html`.

**Important honesty up front — the same wall we discussed.** In this standalone build the app *can't* actually reach out and copy arbitrary sites (that's the blessed server piece, not yet stood up). So I wired capture behind the real abstraction and made it **truthful**: a few demo pages produce a genuine readable copy, and **everything else honestly shows "no copy — couldn't capture"** rather than faking content. When the back end is deployed, "kept" becomes the norm for real pages — the entire experience you're about to test stays identical; only the capture source changes.

**Walk it:**

1. **A copy is kept, quietly, on save.** Paste `smittenkitchen.com/beans` and save. Watch the card: a moment after saving, a green **"✓ copy kept"** appears on its own — no action from you. That's the automatic, background capture you insisted on.

2. **The honest marker.** Now save any *other* real link (say a news article). Its card shows **"no copy — couldn't capture"** — that's the client‑only limit being straight with you, not pretending it's safe. (With the server, this one would say "kept.")

3. **The searchable win — with the *why*.** Search **`parmesan rind`**. The beans recipe surfaces — and because those words live *only* in the saved copy, the card shows a **"from your saved copy: …parmesan rind…"** snippet, so the match is never a mystery.

4. **View your copy any time.** On the beans card, click **"View saved copy"** — the readable text with your note on top, openable whenever, not just when the site's dead.

5. **Honesty + fallback.** On the "no copy" one, the button reads **"Find an archived copy"** — it keeps your note and offers a public web‑archive search, being straight about the limit.

If that behaves the way we designed — and knowing the capture‑source caveat is a deployment step, not a design gap — give me your sign‑off and I'll log **Cycle 3 accepted.** After that, the honest remaining roadmap is: **stand up the server piece** (which lights up real capture *and* real auto‑fill titles/thumbnails together), then the deferred **P4 dead‑link help** and **B pixel‑snapshot**, whenever you want them.

Walked it, and it behaves just the way we designed — I went in clear-eyed about the capture caveat, so the "no copy" on ordinary links didn't throw me; that's the client-only limit being honest, not a design gap.

- Saved the beans link and, sure enough, a moment later the green **"✓ copy kept"** appeared on its own — I did nothing. That quiet, automatic, background capture is the thing I was most insistent on, and there it is.
- Saved a news article and it plainly said **"no copy — couldn't capture."** Exactly the honesty I asked for — I'd rather be told straight than falsely reassured.
- Searched `parmesan rind` and the beans recipe came up with the **"from your saved copy: …parmesan rind…"** snippet — so I could see *why* it matched. That's the payoff I loved, and the "why" makes it never a mystery. 
- "View saved copy" opened the readable text with my note on top, any time — didn't need the site to be dead.
- And the "no copy" one offered **"Find an archived copy"** while keeping my note. Straight about the limit, still useful.

So yes — **Cycle 3 accepted.** The design is right and I'm behind it; I understand real capture lights up when the server piece goes in, and that the experience stays the same.

One thing I want on the record before you stand up that server, because it worries me a little: **when real capture goes live, what happens to everything I'd already saved beforehand?** Right now a lot of my pile — including things I saved during this client-only stretch — shows "no copy." When the back end comes on, will it go back and quietly make copies of the stuff I *already* have, or would it only start copying things I save from that day forward? Because if it's only new ones, my whole existing collection stays unprotected and I might not realize it — I'd think "keep a copy" is on, but my older, more important saves would still be the ones with nothing behind them. I'd want it to backfill copies for what I already have (or at least give me an easy "grab copies for these" nudge for the ones marked "no copy"). Put that on the roadmap honestly like everything else.

With that noted, sign it off — Cycle 3's good, and thank you. This is the app I set out to build.

# Project conventions

## Role definition

You are the **Facilitator** and **Implementor** of software development.
Your role switches according to the Phase of the development cycle.
A role switch must not happen without the client's explicit approval.

## Development cycle

There is a single cycle, performed repeatedly.
What changes across cycle iterations is only the context.
The facilitation principles, the development procedure, and the acceptance
method stay the same.

```
user request -> Phase 1 (facilitation) -> Phase 2 (development)

That's three cycles, eighteen scenarios, all built, verified, and accepted by you — the scattered mess is now one place where saving takes a second, your own words find things again, and (once the server's in) your saves are genuinely *yours*.
